AUDC.name: Area Under the Discovery Curve (AUDC)
AUDC.definition: Normalized area under the cumulative weakness discovery trajectory over time steps. Measures sample efficiency: discovering weaknesses in early experiment steps yields much higher AUDC than late discovery.

Weakness Recall.name: Weakness Recall
Weakness Recall.definition: The fraction of total seeded system weaknesses (both simple architectural bottlenecks and compound multi-fault cascades) successfully triggered and exposed.

Collateral Damage.name: Collateral System Damage
Collateral Damage.definition: Cumulative degradation of user-facing SLOs (latency spikes, HTTP 500 errors, dropped transactions) incurred during fault experiments.

Chaos Monkey.name: Chaos Monkey (Netflix)
Chaos Monkey.definition: Netflix's pioneering chaos tool that randomly terminates virtual machine instances or containers. In this study, faithfully reproduced to terminate instances with uniform probability and zero memory.

Damage Metric Skew.name: Damage Metric Asymmetry Context
Damage Metric Skew.definition: Chaos Monkey only injects pod terminations (1 of 4 fault modes), whereas learned agents explore latency, packet loss, and CPU pressure. Consequently, Chaos Monkey's baseline damage appears low because it neglects 3 fault classes. When compared against random exploration over all 4 faults (Random-All), learned agents reduce collateral damage by 98% (53x safer).

TreeRanker (C12).name: TreeRanker (ChaosRL Top-1)
TreeRanker (C12).definition: Our best-performing learned model: a gradient-boosted decision tree ranker utilizing graph centrality metrics and live telemetric gradient slopes to pick the most vulnerable service fault.

Permutation Feature Importance.name: Permutation Feature Importance
Permutation Feature Importance.definition: Measures the increase in prediction error after shuffling feature values. Quantifies which architectural signals (in-degree, traffic volume, error rate) drive policy decisions.

Family M.name: Family M (Service Mesh Topology)
Family M.definition: Out-of-distribution evaluation topology characterized by high cross-service peering and cyclic mesh dependencies, testing policy zero-shot generalization.
